A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Informed Correctors for Discrete Diffusion Models. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions. v1 Appendices A–B and v2 Appendices A–E were included.

before.justification: v1 reports original countdown simulations, gene-expression generation experiments, and conditional monophonic-music generation results in Section 6.

after.justification: v2 reports original hidden-Markov-model simulations and ImageNet generation experiments in Section 5, plus a Text8 training-objective comparison in Appendix E.

M1.justification: v1's k-Gillespie sampler and symmetrized-rate Barker/MPF correctors are replaced by ancestral prediction with confidence-ranked, parallel Gibbs-style correction that preserves masked positions. v2 also extends the existing hollow transformer with a mixed attention stream and introduces HollowDiff's combined masked/unmasked training-loss estimator. These change sampling, architecture, and training rather than merely renaming the framework.

E1.justification: The countdown process is replaced by a sticky cyclic Markov-chain benchmark with different valid transitions. Gene-expression generation and Lakh monophonic-music continuation are removed. Class-conditional tokenized ImageNet-256 generation and Text8 training/test-loss evaluation are added, substantially changing the represented domains and tasks.

E2.justification: The explicit tau-leaping/k-Gillespie comparisons involving Barker and MPF disappear. v2 adds no-corrector comparisons and evaluates MaskGIT as a sampler on its trained image model in Figure 4; MaskGIT was only discussed in v1. v2 Table 1 also introduces reported comparisons with twelve image-generation models, including VQ-Diffusion, replacing the piano comparison with Campbell et al.

E3.justification: The new synthetic experiment uses exact message-passing denoising probabilities instead of a learned denoiser, with S=4, D=128, stickiness 0.9, and a cosine masking schedule. New ImageNet protocols use a 230M-parameter model, FID/IS/precision/recall, and matched evaluation budgets including a final argmax update. Appendix E adds a separate Text8 training protocol. These are new experimental designs, not demonstrated reruns of retained settings.

E4.justification: v1 examines predictor choice, corrector family, and one versus two correction steps. v2 replaces these analyses with an exact-denoiser failure demonstration and adds ImageNet ablations comparing informed, uninformed, and absent correction on the same model across sampling budgets. Appendix E additionally compares masked-loss training with HollowDiff, directly testing the new objective's convergence benefit.

E5.justification: Both synthetic studies report means and standard deviations over five random seeds. However, v1's gene-expression reporting over 20 runs and piano uncertainty values disappear with those experiments. The new ImageNet table and Text8 loss curves provide no comparable repeated-run uncertainty reporting, reducing its coverage without establishing any increase in runs.

E6.justification: The countdown, gene-expression, and piano results are replaced by new HMM, ImageNet, and Text8 findings. v2 Table 1 reports FID 6.45 for informed correction versus 10.24 without correction and 10.93 with uninformed correction at 17 evaluations; corresponding recall is 0.45 versus 0.52 and 0.51. These are newly reported results under different conditions, not performance improvements over the same v1 experiments.

T1.justification: v1's TauLDR/score-entropy equivalence derivation is retained in v2 Appendix A.1. v2 adds Proposition 3.1 and derivations of the unmasked-position ELBO, combined HollowDiff objective, simplified masked-diffusion score relation, and mask-conditional Gibbs updates in Appendices A.2–B. The earlier Stein-operator construction is removed, substantially revising the mathematical development.

C1.justification: The central claim that informed correction improves sampling efficiency remains. However, v1's headline contribution of k-Gillespie sampling and its cross-domain efficiency claims are replaced by adaptive Gibbs-style correction, a stronger training signal from HollowDiff, and competitive ImageNet generation with fewer evaluations and parameters than the cited diffusion comparators.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations for preserving mask configurations, prioritizing low-confidence tokens, reducing estimator variance through the combined loss, and using a final argmax update to remove residual errors. It also interprets low-budget uninformed correction as less useful than extra prediction steps. The pretrained-model restriction remains, while a limitation concerning large-scale evidence being confined to images is added.

D1.justification: v1 mainly supplies broad parameter counts, A100 hardware, and limited training information. v2 Appendices C–E document attention-stream construction, weight tying, layer dimensions, AdamW settings, batch size, learning-rate schedule, training duration, sampler search grids, and TPU/H100 hardware. This substantially expands implementation and reproducibility information for the revised work.

R1.justification: The central MCMC positioning shifts from Stein operators and Barker/MPF kernels to adaptive random-scan Gibbs sampling, Hogwild updates, and Gumbel-top-k selection, supported by newly cited literature. v2 also develops its relationship to masked-diffusion objectives and positions the image results against MaskGIT and VQ-Diffusion. This goes beyond citation-format or publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and method narrative are substantially rewritten. The separate learning section in v1 is integrated into v2's Methods section, and background and related-work discussions are reorganized. The appendices are restructured into objectives, correctors, architecture, experimental details, and additional results, producing a substantially different document organization.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one column to two columns. The countdown displays and gene-expression bar chart are replaced by a new HMM schematic and error plot, image examples, sampler-FID curves, and Text8 loss curves. Table 1 becomes a grouped image-model comparison with parameter counts and four quality metrics, and the appendices add image galleries.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evaluation and reproducibility: the exact HMM denoiser isolates sampling error, the ImageNet comparisons control the model and evaluation budget, the Text8 ablation tests the new loss, and Appendices C–E supply implementation details largely missing from v1. These gains make the revised claims more testable and reproducible. Removed gene/music coverage, lower recall in the ImageNet ablation, and absent uncertainty estimates for the new large-scale results are material limits, but the stronger controls and documentation support a substantial net improvement.
